title: Counting Bits
statement: Return an array `ans` of length n + 1 where ans[i] is the number of 1-bits in the binary representation of i.
hints: ans[i] = ans[i >> 1] + (i & 1). The shift drops the last bit and the mask reads it.
i & (i - 1) clears the lowest set bit, so ans[i] = ans[i & (i - 1)] + 1 for i > 0.
Either recurrence fills the array in one pass.

approaches.name: DP from the parent number
approaches.explanation: Each integer reuses a smaller answer.

editorial: Right-shifting i produces a number whose popcount is already known, because it is smaller than i. Add one when i is odd. ans[0] is 0. The loop from 1 to n is therefore a linear DP.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def count_bits(n: int) -> list[int]:
    ans = [0] * (n + 1)
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        ans[i] = ans[i >> 1] + (i & 1)
    return ans
